cells.tense: You are standing at a threshold of shared meaning right now, and you know it.
cells.ask: Tell one person close to you what this bond has given you, plainly, today. Let the saying be the whole act.
cells.core:
You're at a threshold and you're not rushing it. Something shared has run its course, or is about to, and you can hold that without turning it into a fight or a quiet exit. You keep caring for what's still alive in it and you stop propping up what isn't — that's the rare part, both at once.

Steady here, the care is clean: you give what the thing actually needs, not what would keep it from changing. That evenness isn't numbness — it's that resting doesn't depend on this resolving first. You could name that out loud, to the person it's about, and lose nothing by it.
cells.sheetLine: You can care for what's here and release what's finished, both at once.
cells.verb: walking on from what was gathered toward the connection that still holds
cells.place: tending what is growing without forcing what it becomes

cells.tense: You are bracing for a leaving that hasn't arrived and may not happen the way you've written it.
cells.ask: Pick one bond you're managing ahead of time and do nothing to shape it for a week. Answer what comes, and let the rest wait.
cells.core:
You're ahead of something. You can feel a change in a shared bond coming, and you've already started preparing for it — pulling back a little, testing the ground, rehearsing the exit before there's anything to leave.

Tended well, this stays in today: you care for the bond as it is and let tomorrow arrive on its own. Right now you're steering it. And that costs you the person. They're being met by your plan for them, not by you. You might be right that something's shifting. Still, a living thing can't be tended by deciding in advance what it will do. Let it show you first, then answer what's actually there.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing a farewell nobody asked for yet.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed, waiting for it to open again.
cells.ask: Say out loud that one thing in a bond has ended. Not to anyone in particular — just so it's said once, in your own hearing.
cells.core:
Something in a shared bond has already changed, and you're caring for it as if it hasn't. You keep showing up for a version of it that isn't there anymore, waiting for it to come back. Tended well, your care moves with what's actually in the room. Here the aim is off by one season.

It isn't that you missed a signal. Walking on from something you love feels like abandoning it, so you stay put. But you can't tend what's growing while you guard what's gone. You don't have to feel ready. Look at what's here, let your care follow that, and say the ending once so it stops being a secret you keep from yourself.
cells.sheetLine: You're caring for something that already changed shape.

cells.tense: You are already tending this bond carefully, and you're describing it as just being practical.
cells.ask: Name one thing you do for someone because it matters to you, and you've been calling it logistics, favors, or just handling it.
cells.core:
The check-ins, the remembering, the way you adjust what you say so someone can hear it — that's care for what's growing, and it's shaping how this bond holds. You call it being sensible, or just how you are. Steady here, you know it's yours and you pick it on purpose.

The work is already running. What's missing is you saying it's yours. Left automatic, it can't be rested from or changed, because you didn't claim to be doing it — and that's not a small thing to keep from yourself. Naming it as yours hands the pen back. That's the whole ask. The rest you already have.
cells.sheetLine: The care is yours. You've been calling it just being practical.
